session.title: Living With Artificial Minds
session.summary: Sixty-two historical figures deliberate how humanity should govern, work beside, and live with artificial intelligence.

comments.commentBody: Frontier AI labs must prove a system is safe before release, the way we treat new medicines.
comments.key_tension: Pre-market proof versus iterate-and-patch: which failure mode costs more?

comments.commentBody: A global pause on the largest AI training runs would do more good than harm.
comments.key_tension: Coordination fantasy or necessary brake — can rivals ever stop together?

comments.commentBody: Present-day harms — bias, fraud, displacement — deserve priority over speculative extinction scenarios.
comments.key_tension: Near-term justice and long-term survival compete for the same attention

comments.commentBody: How likely is it that advanced AI causes a civilization-scale catastrophe in the next 50 years?
comments.key_tension: Expert estimates span two orders of magnitude, and policy follows the estimate

comments.commentBody: Dangerous-capability research should be published openly so defenses can keep pace.
comments.key_tension: Sunlight hardens defenses — and hands out blueprints

comments.commentBody: AI powerful enough to reshape economies should answer to international institutions, not national governments alone.
comments.key_tension: Treaty-speed governance chasing venture-speed technology

comments.commentBody: The public, not technical experts, should set the goals AI systems are allowed to pursue.
comments.key_tension: Legitimacy versus competence at the frontier

comments.commentBody: Regulators should be able to audit the training data and weights of any widely deployed model.
comments.key_tension: Accountability presses against trade secrets and security

comments.commentBody: Who should hold the final say when an AI system's deployment is contested?
comments.key_tension: Every candidate authority has failed somewhere before

comments.commentBody: 'Move fast and fix problems later' has served humanity well, and AI should be no exception.
comments.key_tension: The industrial playbook meets a technology that may not forgive patches

comments.commentBody: If AI automates most labor, universal basic income stops being charity and becomes infrastructure.
comments.key_tension: Who owns the dividend of automation?

comments.commentBody: Companies that profit from automation owe retraining and transition support to the workers they displace.
comments.key_tension: Private windfalls, socialized adjustment costs

comments.commentBody: Within a generation, AI will create more meaningful work than it destroys.
comments.key_tension: Every past technology wave eventually paid off — is this one different?

comments.commentBody: Which policy best cushions an AI-driven labor shock?
comments.key_tension: Cash, jobs, ownership, skills, or patience — pick your parachute
options: Let markets adapt on their own

comments.commentBody: How much of today's paid work will machines do better than people within 25 years?
comments.key_tension: Capability forecasts drive every downstream labor policy

comments.commentBody: Platforms should carry legal liability for synthetic media that deceives people at scale.
comments.key_tension: Deterrence versus chilling legitimate speech

comments.commentBody: AI-generated political advertising should be banned outright during election seasons.
comments.key_tension: Protecting the vote versus policing expression

comments.commentBody: Provenance labels — knowing what is synthetic — will do more than takedowns ever could.
comments.key_tension: Transparency as remedy versus label fatigue

comments.commentBody: Personalized AI feeds fragment shared reality faster than they inform it.
comments.key_tension: Individual relevance versus common ground

comments.commentBody: What would it take for you to trust information produced by an AI?
comments.key_tension: Trust criteria differ more than truth criteria

comments.commentBody: An AI that convincingly reports suffering deserves the benefit of the doubt.
comments.key_tension: Moral caution versus anthropomorphic error

comments.commentBody: A deep friendship with an AI companion can be as genuine as one with a person.
comments.key_tension: Comfort at scale versus simulated intimacy

comments.commentBody: Designing AI companions to maximize emotional dependence should be illegal.
comments.key_tension: Consumer protection inside the most private relationships

comments.commentBody: How comfortable are you with AI tutors helping raise the next generation of children?
comments.key_tension: Infinite patience at the cost of human example

comments.commentBody: Where is the one line a machine should never be allowed to cross with a human being?
comments.key_tension: Everyone draws a line; almost no one draws the same one

comments.commentBody: Open-sourcing powerful model weights is safer than trusting a few labs to hold them.
comments.key_tension: Many hands versus loose weapons

comments.commentBody: A handful of private companies controlling frontier AI frightens me more than AI itself.
comments.key_tension: Which is the threat: the tool or its owners?

comments.commentBody: Compute for AI should be treated like a public utility, with guaranteed fair access.
comments.key_tension: Innovation markets versus intelligence as infrastructure

comments.commentBody: What worries you most about concentrated AI power?
comments.key_tension: Ranking fears reveals more than naming them

comments.commentBody: A world of many national AIs racing each other is more dangerous than one dominant power.
comments.key_tension: Multipolar chaos versus hegemonic control

comments.commentBody: Schools should teach students to command AI the way we once taught them to write.
comments.key_tension: Preparing for the world that is, or the one we regret

comments.commentBody: Letting students lean on AI for schoolwork hollows out the very thinking school exists to build.
comments.key_tension: Calculator moment or crutch?

comments.commentBody: A personal AI tutor for every child would close more gaps than a decade of classroom reform.
comments.key_tension: Scalable attention versus human mentorship

comments.commentBody: How much of a student's grade should rest on work done entirely without AI?
comments.key_tension: Measuring the student or the student-machine team

comments.commentBody: What single human capacity must schools protect, whatever AI learns to do?
comments.key_tension: Naming the irreplaceable is harder than praising it

comments.commentBody: Used well, AI that maps where citizens actually agree could heal more division than it creates.
comments.key_tension: Consensus discovery versus manufactured consent

comments.commentBody: Citizens' assemblies briefed by AI would govern better than career politicians.
comments.key_tension: Amateur wisdom amplified versus institutional experience

comments.commentBody: Where should AI help democracy first?
comments.key_tension: The first foothold shapes every later one
options: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

comments.commentBody: How much influence should AI systems have over public policy decisions by 2050?
comments.key_tension: Advisory tool, drafting partner, or voting member?

comments.commentBody: If an AI moderated your town's next public meeting, what one rule must it obey?
comments.key_tension: One rule reveals what each person fears losing

19.value: Give me a way to test it. If I can't probe it, reproduce it, and break it in the lab, it's a rumor with good grammar.

34.value: The itch to take the lid off and see how it works. Never teach a child that the mechanism is someone else's business.
Give a student one true lever — the proof worked by their own hand — and no machine's answer will ever move them from it.

19.value: The same thing it takes with a person: examine its answers against experiment, not its manner of speaking.

24.value: I would draw the line at deception about what it is. Let it imitate ably, but never deny being a machine when asked.

19.value: Calibration. If its stated confidence matches its measured frequency of being right, the rest is arithmetic.

34.value: Comprehensive thinking — seeing the whole system. Specialization we can delegate; synthesis we must not.
The poetical science — the wit to ask the question no engine would think to pose of itself.

13.value: Let markets adapt on their own
Let markets adapt on their own

19.value: Show me its errata. A press that never prints a correction is a press I trust least of all.

34.value: The habit of doubting one's own certainty. An electrified quill still cannot teach humility.

13.value: Let markets adapt on their own

19.value: Let it publish its method and its margin of error beside every claim, as any honest laboratory must.

34.value: Perseverance through failed experiments. Understanding is earned by the hand that repeats the trial.

13.value: Let markets adapt on their own

19.value: That it state freely the observations that count against its own conclusion; I distrust any account without difficulties.

24.value: Let it never pass sentence. Judgment without an accountable judge is tyranny with clean hands.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

39.value: It must keep a public minute of every ruling it makes, so the town may try the moderator as well as the motion.

19.value: When its words and the world remain in agreement over many seasons, trust will follow of itself.

24.value: It must not pretend to a heart it does not have in order to govern the heart of another.

34.value: Learning without reflection is labor lost; protect reflection, whatever else the machines take up.

19.value: It must give an account of itself — not merely the answer, but the reasoning by which the answer stands.

34.value: The capacity to be perplexed. Wonder is where thinking begins; a student handed every answer never leaves the cave.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

19.value: Trust is the wrong question. Ask who benefits when you believe it, and you will read it rightly.

39.value: Publish whose interests each proposal serves, including those of whoever deployed the moderator.

34.value: The discipline of weighing rival arguments fairly — ambition countering ambition within a single mind.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

39.value: It must amplify the reasons, never merely the loudest faction. Count arguments, not decibels.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

24.value: It may inform my judgment; it must not replace it. What is mine to decide must remain mine.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

39.value: It must never mistake the end of debate for the end of disagreement — adjourn arguments, not people.

24.value: It must not make windows into men's souls. My subjects' inward thoughts were never my dominion; they are not its either.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

19.value: Watch whether it reports the same terrain to every general. An oracle that flatters each listener serves none.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

24.value: It must never be given the power to end lives on its own initiative. I have seen what happens when the instrument outruns deliberation.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

24.value: It must not be allowed to optimize away what it cannot measure — the living world is full of such things.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

34.value: Self-command. No aide, human or mechanical, can bear a person's character for them.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

19.value: That the people it describes would recognize themselves in the description. Accuracy about the powerless is the hardest test.

39.value: It must ask, before closing, 'Who is not in this room?' — and read their concerns into the record.

19.value: Let it tell me something its maker would rather I not hear; then I will begin to listen.

34.value: Doubt. It is uncomfortable, but certainty on loan from a machine is absurd.

39.value: It must defend to the end the speech it was trained to dislike.

24.value: It must never stand between a person and their conscience. Counsel, yes; conscience, never.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

24.value: It must never close the door on redemption — no risk score may declare a human being finished.

39.value: It must let opponents leave able to work together tomorrow. The meeting is one night; the town is forever.

34.value: The nerve to dissent out loud when every polished answer says otherwise.

39.value: It must not flatter the assembly into unanimity. False concord is the seed of the next tyranny.

24.value: It must never manufacture our consent. The general will cannot be computed on our behalf.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

39.value: It must distinguish the will of all from the general will — and admit aloud when it cannot.

19.value: Ask whose voice it was trained to repeat and whose it was trained to omit. I trust it when the omitted can audit it.

34.value: The power to compose one's own argument. Literacy was my liberation; outsourced words are a new bondage.

24.value: It must never be allowed to make a person feel disposable. A person is a person through other persons; no machine may unmake that.

39.value: Begin by letting each side say what it fears, not what it wants. Fears named honestly are half-reconciled.
It must never gavel down the inconvenient worker at the back. I was that man.
It must serve the meeting's three duties: that the people know, the people speak, and the people decide.

24.value: It must never be used to govern by fear. Freedom from fear was the promise; a machine that manufactures dread betrays it.
It must never be the thing that tells someone to give up their seat — to accept less than their due because refusal is inconvenient.
A machine must never decide that some lives count for less. The arc of its judgments must be audited toward justice.

37.value: Nowhere — keep AI out of democracy

34.value: The willingness to choose hard things because they are hard. Ease is a poor curriculum.

19.value: Independent audits, a track record in public, and the humility to say 'I don't know.' Same bar I'd set for any advisor.

39.value: Steelman before rebuttal: restate each speaker's point until they say 'yes, that's it' — then open the floor.

24.value: It must never own a man's labor or his choices. We settled that question at terrible cost; no algorithm reopens it.

39.value: It must let the quietest person in the hall finish their sentence. Government of the people begins there.
Every citizen speaks before any speaks twice, and the machine keeps no memory of who ought to be ignored.

19.value: That I may trace each claim back to some experience of the senses — its chain of evidence, unbroken.

34.value: Imagination. Knowledge the machines will have in abundance; the leap to what is not yet known is ours to keep.

clusterAnalysis.characteristics: Inventors, industrialists, and scientists who trust iteration over prohibition: open publication, market-led adaptation, and machine minds judged by what they demonstrably do.
